items.title: Google Releases Core Update Targeting Discover Feed
items.summary: Google has launched the February 2026 Discover core update, a broad change to systems surfacing content in the Discover feed, initially for English-language users in the U.S., with plans to expand to other countries and languages over the coming months. The update aims to show more locally relevant content from websites based in users' countries, reduce sensational content and clickbait, and prioritize in-depth, original, and timely content from sites with expertise in given areas. It began rolling out on Feb. 5 and may take up to two weeks, with advice to monitor Discover traffic separately from organic search in Search Console and focus on improving content quality.

items.title: Google Says Links Will Be More Visible In AI Overviews
items.summary: Google is updating AI Overviews and AI Mode by adding hover link pop-ups on desktop that display site names, favicons, and short descriptions when users hover over groups of links. Link icons will also be more descriptive and prominent across desktop and mobile responses. This change aims to make it easier to access content across the web, potentially addressing concerns about reduced link clicks in AI summaries, which have seen CTR drops.

items.title: Google AI Shows A Site Is Offline Due To JS Content Delivery
items.summary: A site owner reported Google AI Search incorrectly stating their site was offline since early 2026, but Google's John Mueller identified the cause as improper JavaScript where placeholder text like 'not available' was replaced only after JS execution, leading to misleading indexing. Mueller advised loading content directly in the base HTML to ensure consistent delivery for users and crawlers, avoiding non-JS fallback errors. This case underscores technical SEO risks with dynamic JS, emphasizing static initial HTML for accurate crawling.

items.title: AI didn’t kill SEO. It killed average content.
items.summary: Generative AI has not eliminated SEO but has made average or 'good enough' content obsolete, as it floods the web with low-value material that search engines deprioritize. Brands must now create authentic, defensible content using proprietary data, novel frameworks, expert insights, and human elements to build authority amid AI saturation and falling CTRs. The focus shifts to net new value and minimalism, avoiding volume tactics that cause cannibalization.

items.title: Google’s AI search results will make links more obvious
items.summary: Google is enhancing link prominence in AI Overviews and AI Mode with desktop hover pop-ups showing descriptions and images of cited sources, plus more descriptive link icons on mobile and desktop. VP Robby Stein noted testing shows higher engagement, helping users access web content more easily. This addresses publisher concerns over AI-driven traffic loss amid regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Controversy Surrounding Pseudonymous Author Coral Hart and Generative AI in Romance Novels
items.summary: A controversy has emerged involving the pseudonymous author Coral Hart, highlighted by a New York Times article on her use of generative AI to produce numerous quick romance novels for profit. Hart offers online courses and sells customizable prefabricated novels for hundreds of dollars, claiming to be an international bestselling and award-winning author without providing proof. The update warns aspiring authors against paying for her services, urging them to seek free advice from real authors instead.

items.title: This publisher enlists 'bookfluencers' to choose its titles. Is it working?
items.summary: Bindery Books, a San Francisco-based publishing startup, employs a model where bookfluencers serve as acquiring editors for its imprints, integrating reader input to champion underrepresented authors and debut titles, including many unagented ones. In speculative fiction, influencer Kathryn Budig's Inky Phoenix imprint has successfully promoted titles leveraging online communities. The innovative approach draws on Bookstagram and BookTok trends, though the company remains unprofitable.

items.title: What Do You Do When the Biggest Platforms For Readers Are Kind of Evil?
items.summary: The article explores ethical dilemmas for readers and authors using platforms like RELX (organizer of BookCon) and Spotify (audiobook giant) due to their ties to controversial government contracts like ICE. Speculative fiction author Alix E. Harrow criticizes such corporate involvement and calls for divestment. It highlights ongoing tradeoffs and successful boycotts in the publishing world.

items.title: New Book Releases: February 17, 2026
items.summary: Locus Magazine highlights new speculative fiction releases including Heather Fawcett’s fantasy Agnes Aubert’s Mystical Cat Shelter set in 1920s Montreal, Kate Golden’s Half City about a demon hunter at an academy, and Nnedi Okorafor’s novella The Daughter Who Remains. These titles represent fresh voices in fantasy. The weekly list covers the science fiction, fantasy, and horror fields.

items.title: Letter from a Reader 2.17.26: Publishers' Loss of Decency
items.summary: Publishers face criticism for minimal responses to scandals involving fabricated memoirs like Raynor Winn’s The Salt Path, offering no refunds or proper apologies. Books now enjoy longer promotional runways thanks to digital formats amid rising competition. Spy novelists struggle to match John le Carré, with new titles like David McCloskey’s The Persian emerging.

items.title: Emerald Fennell's 'Wuthering Heights' Hits $92M Box Office, Surpasses 'Zodiac'
items.summary: Emerald Fennell's bold adaptation of Emily Brontë's gothic romance, starring Margot Robbie as Catherine Earnshaw and Jacob Elordi as Heathcliff, has grossed $92 million worldwide in its first five days since the February 13, 2026 release. The film recouped its $80 million budget during the opening weekend and overtook David Fincher's 'Zodiac' lifetime earnings, drawing massive female audiences despite mixed 60% Rotten Tomatoes reviews.

items.title: 'Off Campus' TV Series Announces Key Castings for Prime Video Premiere
items.summary: Prime Video's adaptation of Elle Kennedy’s hockey romance novels casts Ella Bright as Hannah Wells and Belmont Cameli as Garrett Graham in the story of Briar University's ice hockey team romances. With additional stars like Josh Heuston and Antonio Cipriano, the series has early Season 2 renewal and targets a May 2026 debut for Season 1. February 17 updates fuel anticipation for this steamy book-to-screen project.

items.title: Apple TV+ Drops Teaser for 'Imperfect Women' Starring Moss, Washington, Mara
items.summary: The psychological thriller series, adapting Araminta Hall’s novel about friends unraveling after a death, features Elisabeth Moss, Kerry Washington, and Kate Mara. Created by Annie Weisman, the eight-episode run premieres March 18, 2026, with the first two episodes available then, followed weekly. The recent teaser builds hype for this tense book adaptation.

items.title: 'The Last Thing He Told Me' Season 2 Premieres Today on Apple TV+
items.summary: Laura Dave’s sequel novel inspires Season 2 of the thriller series starring Jennifer Garner, with Judy Greer joining the cast for more family secrets and suspense. Premiering February 20, 2026, on Apple TV+, it follows the concurrent book adaptation's second chapter. This week's release marks a major return for book-to-screen fans.

items.title: Tri Counties Bank Releases Study on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its Impact on Small Businesses
items.summary: The Tri Counties Bank study reveals that 73% of U.S. small business owners currently use AI, with 20% employing it extensively and 14% planning to adopt it, primarily to boost productivity, automate tasks, and enhance profitability. Key stats show 83% expect a favorable business impact, with anticipated labor cost savings of 6–20% mainly for full-time and part-time staff. Small business owners can gain efficiency and growth by adopting AI in back-office functions like marketing and document management.

items.title: How AI Is Helping Small Retailers Take On Big-Box Giants
items.summary: AI lowers the cost and complexity of personalization, operations, and omnichannel execution for small retailers, enabling enterprise-level capabilities like personalized outreach, smarter inventory management, and consistent product descriptions without large teams. It amplifies human connections by automating back-office tasks, freeing staff to focus on tailored recommendations and relationships that big-box stores struggle to replicate. Trends show 58% of small businesses using generative AI.

items.title: Want To Grow Revenue In A Small Business? This Study Suggests That Adopting AI Can Help
items.summary: A Gusto study shows small businesses with higher AI adoption see revenue growth, with a 10 percentage point increase in AI exposure predicting about 2.2% higher monthly revenue six months later. Higher AI use also correlates with slight employment increases, countering job loss fears. Tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude help with research, operations, and product development.

items.title: Small Business Technology News: AI Models That Are Better Than ChatGPT
items.summary: New AI models outperform ChatGPT in research and coding, while Intuit expands AI in QuickBooks with fintech integrations for small businesses. LinkedIn's agentic AI Hiring Assistant cuts recruitment time, and Newo offers AI front-desk agents for calls and appointments. These tools boost efficiency in finance, hiring, and customer service for entrepreneurs.
